Reports had earlier suggested Apple had scrapped its long-rumoured all-glass iPhone project marking the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, but according to the latest reporting from Bloomberg, the redesign is still on track for next year's Pro models. Details below.

Bloomberg says the redesign is still on track

Investment research firm Jefferies earlier today downgraded Apple's stock, citing supply-chain findings indicating that Apple had abandoned plans to release an all-glass iPhone next year to mark the 20th anniversary of the device.

According to Bloomberg's latest report, the company "is expected to release an iPhone Pro model next year with a new glass-like finish," adding that "the phone will feature glass on the front and back (with internal code names V73 and V74, respectively), with the material extending around the sides, connected by a metal frame in the middle."

However, the report also notes that the project has been modified since its original conception:

The report goes further to directly refute Jefferies' earlier note, stating that "Apple's product roadmap remains unchanged."

What Jefferies said

Earlier today, Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said that, based on the firm's supply-chain checks, the all-glass iPhone had been cancelled due to poor production yields.

Lee described the development as a "significant setback" for Apple's push to premiumise the iPhone amid rising memory costs, adding that cancelling the plan could hurt Apple's ability to raise the average selling price and margin on Pro models.

Jefferies accordingly downgraded Apple's stock and cut its target price from US$285.56 to US$263.66, having previously trimmed it from US$308.92 on July 31 after Apple reported fiscal third-quarter 2026 results and issued cautious guidance for the fourth quarter.
